sentences.en: Americans have long expressed their political views with their wallets.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，美国人一直用钱包表达他们的政治观点。

sentences.en: In recent months, this has ramped up with boycotts and with boycotts.
sentences.zh: 最近几个月，抵制和支持消费的现象愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: That's where people express support by buying a company's products.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们通过购买某家公司的产品来表达支持的方式。

sentences.en: For months now, Nordstrom has been on a list of Trump-affiliated companies to boycott.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，诺德斯特龙一直被列入特朗普相关被抵制公司的名单中。

sentences.en: This is just, it's a wonderful line.
sentences.zh: 这真的是，这是一句非常棒的话。

sentences.en: I fully, I'm going to just give it, I'm going to give a free commercial here.
sentences.zh: 我完全，我打算直接说出来，我在这里做一个免费广告。

sentences.en: I deleted Uber recently due to what happened at JFK Airport
sentences.zh: 我最近由于肯尼迪国际机场发生的事情删除了优步，

sentences.en: when it appeared that Uber was essentially trying to break the strike.
sentences.zh: 当时看起来优步基本上是在试图破坏罢工。

sentences.en: Fueled the outrage and led to some people to call for a boycott of the airline.
sentences.zh: 这引发了愤怒，并导致一些人呼吁抵制该航空公司。

sentences.en: It seems like people are a little fed up and disillusioned with sort of conventional political channels
sentences.zh: 似乎人们对那种传统的政治渠道已经有些厌倦和幻灭了，

sentences.en: where they would normally sort of express their political views.
sentences.zh: 在过去，他们通常会在那里表达自己的政治观点。

sentences.en: And so in the absence of that legitimacy, there's been sort of a rise in political consumerism.
sentences.zh: 因此，在缺乏这种合法性的情况下，政治消费主义开始兴起。

sentences.en: Neeru Paharia is a marketing professor at Georgetown University.
sentences.zh: 尼鲁·帕哈里亚是乔治城大学的市场营销教授。

sentences.en: She studies how consumer behavior often serves psychological needs rather than economic needs.
sentences.zh: 她研究消费者行为如何往往服务于心理需求而非经济需求。

sentences.en: When we think about the way we spend money, we may think about the comfort of a nice pair of shoes
sentences.zh: 当我们思考我们花钱的方式时，我们可能会想到一双好鞋带来的舒适感，

sentences.en: or the pleasure of a great meal.
sentences.zh: 或者一顿美食带来的快乐。

sentences.en: But money also serves a deeper purpose.
sentences.zh: 但金钱也服务于更深层的目的。

sentences.en: We use money to express our feelings, to project our status, to defend our values.
sentences.zh: 我们用金钱来表达感受、彰显地位、捍卫价值观。

sentences.en: The products we buy tell stories.
sentences.zh: 我们购买的产品讲述着故事。
我们讲给别人听的故事。
我们讲给自己听的故事。

sentences.en: For a small coffee shop, people don't really think much of the political situation.
sentences.zh: 对于一家小咖啡馆，人们其实并不会太在意政治形势。

sentences.en: But as soon as you put a large competitor in next door, say you put a Starbucks in next door,
sentences.zh: 但一旦你在旁边开了一家大型竞争对手，比方说在隔壁开了一家星巴克，

sentences.en: all of a sudden it becomes this fight between the little guy and the big guy.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，这就演变成了小人物与大人物之间的战斗。

sentences.en: Neeru Paharia says she first became interested in the psychological power of consumer products
sentences.zh: 尼鲁·帕哈里亚说她最初对消费品的心理力量产生兴趣，

sentences.en: How else could two months' salary last forever?
sentences.zh: 还有什么能让两个月的薪水维持到永远？

sentences.en: I studied economics as an undergraduate.
And one thing they tell you as an economics major is that people are rational.
sentences.zh: 经济学专业教给你的第一件事就是人是理性的。

sentences.en: But as far as Neeru could tell, there was nothing particularly rational about buying a diamond.
sentences.zh: 但在尼鲁看来，买钻石这事儿怎么看都不怎么理性。

sentences.en: Now, you can argue that diamonds are beautiful, but there are cheaper stones that are just as pretty.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以争辩说钻石很漂亮，但也有更便宜且同样漂亮的石头。

sentences.en: So then the question is, why are people spending so much money on these shiny rocks that have no intrinsic value?
sentences.zh: 所以问题来了，为什么人们要花这么多钱买这些毫无内在价值闪闪发光的石头？

sentences.en: You know, there's effectively a perfect substitute.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，实际上存在着完美的替代品。

sentences.en: And then it seemed like it was all this kind of psychological stuff that people wanted to express their status.
sentences.zh: 然后这就好像所有这些都是人们想要表达自己地位的心理把戏。

sentences.en: People wanted to kind of fit in with sort of the normative practices in terms of marriage.
sentences.zh: 人们希望融入某种关于婚姻的规范化习俗中。

sentences.en: And it's just sort of dawned on me that products have all this psychological value, and that's worth real money.
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到产品具有所有的心理价值，而这是值真金白银的。

sentences.en: I mean, a whole industry is based on just sort of pure kind of signaling and psychological value.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个行业仅仅建立在纯粹的符号象征和心理价值之上。

sentences.en: And I found that to be really interesting and sort of at odds with this notion that people are rational.
sentences.zh: 我发现这真的很有趣，而且与“人是理性的”这种观点相矛盾。

sentences.en: This idea made Neeru think about the other ways we use money as a signaling device to express our beliefs and our values.
sentences.zh: 这个想法让尼鲁开始思考我们使用金钱作为信号装置来表达我们的信仰和价值观的其他方式。

sentences.en: We enact our political will usually by voting or supporting different kinds of legislations and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们通常通过投票或支持各种立法之类的事情来行使我们的政治意愿。

sentences.en: So it's kind of interesting when people start taking that civic actions, these kind of civic actions into the market,
sentences.zh: 所以当人们开始把这种公民行动带入市场时，这就变得很有趣了，

sentences.en: and then start boycotting or boycotting a certain brand or a certain company in order to express their view.
sentences.zh: 然后开始抵制或支持某个品牌或某家公司以表达他们的观点。

sentences.en: And you can kind of think about it in terms of what ends up being more tangible.
sentences.zh: 你可以从什么最终更切实的角度来思考这个问题。

sentences.en: So if we think about voting, it's sort of an abstract process.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们想想投票，那是一种抽象的过程。

sentences.en: Whereas when you buy a product or avoid buying a product, it's very tangible.
sentences.zh: 而当你购买产品或避免购买产品时，它是非常切实的。

sentences.en: If you're someone who doesn't buy flashy jewelry, you may say,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个不买浮夸珠宝的人，你可能会说，

sentences.en: OK, I'm not one of those people who uses money to talk.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不是那种用金钱说话的人。

sentences.en: Or maybe you just don't use diamonds to talk.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你只是不用钻石说话。

sentences.en: I've studied the situations between small coffee shops and large coffee shops.
sentences.zh: 我研究了小型咖啡馆和大型咖啡馆之间的情况。

sentences.en: And so I have a paper where we show that for a small coffee shop, if it's just sitting there by itself,
sentences.zh: 因此我有一篇论文，我们在其中展示了对于一家小型咖啡馆，如果它只是独自开在那里，

sentences.en: people don't really think much of the political situation.
sentences.zh: 人们其实不会多想政治形势。

sentences.en: They just think more about the coffee, sort of about the more rational economic features and attributes of the product.
sentences.zh: 他们更多地考虑咖啡，考虑产品更理性的经济特征和属性。

sentences.en: But as soon as you put a large competitor in next door, say you put a Starbucks in next door,
sentences.zh: 但一旦你在隔壁引入了一个大型竞争对手，比方说在隔壁开了一家星巴克，

sentences.en: all of a sudden it becomes this fight between the little guy and the big guy.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，这就变成了一场小人物与大人物之间的战斗。

sentences.en: And then buying your cup of coffee is really meaningful.
sentences.zh: 然后你买的那杯咖啡就真的变得意义重大了。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, it's a symbol of what you believe in.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，它成了你信仰的象征。

sentences.en: It's a symbol of you supporting the little guy, of you supporting the underdog and trying to stick it to the man.
sentences.zh: 它是你支持小人物、支持弱者并试图对抗强权的象征。

sentences.en: And I just find it so fascinating that that's sort of how we kind of we kind of express our political views on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这太迷人了，这正是我们在日常生活中表达政治观点的方式。

sentences.en: And we feel, you know, powerful in a sense that we actually sort of have a say in the situation.
sentences.zh: 而且我们感到，你知道的，在某种意义上很强大，因为我们实际上对局势有了一定的发言权。

sentences.en: Companies, of course, pay attention to what consumers want.
sentences.zh: 公司当然会关注消费者想要什么。

sentences.en: They understand that people don't just want to buy a cup of coffee or a computer.
sentences.zh: 他们明白人们不只是想买一杯咖啡或一台电脑。

sentences.en: They want the right story to go with that cup of coffee or computer.
sentences.zh: 他们想要与那杯咖啡或电脑相匹配的正确故事。

sentences.en: This is why so many Silicon Valley companies that are worth billions of dollars
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么许多价值数十亿美元的硅谷公司

sentences.en: spend so much time telling us about their origin stories,
sentences.zh: 花大量时间向我们讲述他们的起源故事，

sentences.en: how two kids dropped out of college to explore a dream in someone's garage.
sentences.zh: 比如两个孩子如何从大学辍学，在某个人的车库里探索梦想。

sentences.en: So this is what we call, we have another paper around underdog brand biographies,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们所说的，我们还有另一篇关于弱者品牌传记的论文，

sentences.en: and the sort of idea of kind of starting in a garage from humble beginnings,
sentences.zh: 以及那种从车库起步、出身卑微的想法，

sentences.en: but overcoming obstacles to kind of fulfill your dream.
sentences.zh: 但通过克服重重困难来最终实现你的梦想。

sentences.en: That's a really compelling narrative, especially to Americans.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常引人入胜的故事，对美国人来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: I think because of the whole kind of pull yourself up from your bootstraps
sentences.zh: 我想是因为那种靠自己白手起家的精神

sentences.en: and this whole notion of the American dream.
sentences.zh: 以及美国梦的整个概念。

sentences.en: And so companies that take advantage of that narrative,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些利用这种叙事的公司，

sentences.en: and if they use it effectively, even as they grow,
sentences.zh: 如果他们能有效地运用它，即使在他们成长之后，

sentences.en: can kind of remind consumers that, you know, this was a small company
sentences.zh: 也可以提醒消费者，你知道的，这曾是一家小公司，

sentences.en: and they might, you know, identify with it more
sentences.zh: 他们可能会，你知道的，对它更有认同感，

sentences.en: and thus, you know, like penalize them less for being a large company.
sentences.zh: 从而，你知道的，因为体量庞大而受到的惩罚就会减少。

sentences.en: There tends to be sort of a kind of an aversion or a disdain for large companies.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对大公司有一种厌恶或鄙视的情绪。

sentences.en: People tend to identify a lot more with smaller companies.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对小公司的认同感要高得多。

sentences.en: And you tell the story of Nantucket Nectars,
sentences.zh: 你讲了楠塔基特花蜜的故事，

sentences.en: which also has the same sort of startup story.
sentences.zh: 它也有着同样的创业故事。

sentences.en: A lot of companies, they talk about how Nantucket Nectars in particular
sentences.zh: 许多公司，它们谈论楠塔基特花蜜尤其如此，

sentences.en: talks about how they started with a blender and a dream,
sentences.zh: 谈论他们是如何从一个搅拌机和一个梦想开始的，

sentences.en: and Cliff Bar talks about how, you know, they started in their garage with,
sentences.zh: 克里夫能量棒也谈到，你知道的，他们是在车库里开始的，

sentences.en: he was living with his dog and his skis and, you know, was cooking.
sentences.zh: 当时他带着狗、滑雪板生活，你知道的，还在做饭。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's this sort of underdog narrative
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，正是这种弱者叙事

sentences.en: that makes use of this sort of external disadvantage,
but really, you know, trying hard.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道的，一直在努力奋斗。

sentences.en: And I think people really, really find that story resonating
sentences.zh: 我想人们真的、真的很能产生共鸣，

sentences.en: because I think we all on some level feel like underdogs.
sentences.zh: 因为我想我们在某种程度上都觉得自己是弱者。

sentences.en: And so it sort of is can be motivating to us.
sentences.zh: 所以它在某种程度上可以激励我们。

sentences.en: Companies are also extremely skilled at selling us things
sentences.zh: 公司也非常擅长向我们销售

sentences.en: that are tied to a certain sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 与某种身份认同感挂钩的东西。

sentences.en: I remember this set of ads that Apple was running some years ago
sentences.zh: 我记得苹果公司几年前播放过的一系列广告，

sentences.en: where they basically suggested that people who bought Macs
sentences.zh: 它们基本上暗示购买Mac的人

sentences.en: were hipper and cooler than people who bought PCs.
sentences.zh: 比购买PC的人更时髦、更酷。

sentences.en: Well, I was sitting on my desk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时正放在桌子上。

sentences.en: Someone walked by, carelessly tripped over my power cord,
sentences.zh: 有人路过，不小心绊到了我的电源线，

sentences.en: yanked me straight down to the ground.
MacBooks come with this power cord that connects magnetically,
sentences.zh: MacBook配备了这种磁吸连接的电源线，

sentences.en: so when it gets pulled, it just pops right off.
sentences.zh: 所以当它被拉扯时，就会直接脱落。

sentences.en: Everything is just kind of thought out, you know,
sentences.zh: 一切都是经过深思熟虑的，你知道的，

sentences.en: like the tiny built-in eyesight camera.
My life is flashing before my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我的一生正在我眼前闪现。

sentences.en: I see a sunset in a field of beautiful wheat.
sentences.zh: 我看到一片美丽小麦田里的日落。
那不就是你的屏幕保护程序吗？

sentences.en: They were basically saying if you buy this kind of computer,
sentences.zh: 它们基本上是在说，如果你买这种电脑，

sentences.en: it sends a signal of the kind of person you are.
sentences.zh: 它就会传递出你是什么样的人的信号。

sentences.en: It's not so much about your status but how cool you are.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是关于你的身份地位，不如说是关于你有多酷。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think being cool is also a form of status, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我认为很酷也是一种身份地位，你知道的。

sentences.en: You want to, you want to, and there's actually recent research on this
sentences.zh: 你想要，你想要，沃伦和坎贝尔最近实际上对此有研究，

sentences.en: by Warren and Campbell, and they talk about how coolness is essentially
sentences.zh: 他们谈到酷本质上是如何

sentences.en: another way of kind of signaling your status,
sentences.zh: 标榜你社会地位的另一种方式，

sentences.en: which can be very compelling to certain groups of consumers
sentences.zh: 这对某些消费者群体非常有吸引力，

sentences.en: who want to signal their autonomy, that they're not just drones
sentences.zh: 他们想要彰显自己的独立性，表明他们不只是随波逐流的机器，

sentences.en: and just kind of following the masses, but that they're autonomous,
sentences.zh: 不只是盲目跟风大众，而是他们具有独立性，

sentences.en: that they have kind of control and are kind of independently minded.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有某种控制力并且思想相当独立。

sentences.en: There is some irony here in an advertising campaign by a major company
sentences.zh: 这里存在某种讽刺意味：一家大公司的广告活动

sentences.en: trying to convince people that if you buy products made by that company,
sentences.zh: 试图说服人们，如果你购买该公司制造的产品，

sentences.en: you're actually acting independently and autonomously,
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在独立自主地行动，

sentences.en: when in fact the advertising is actually making you do
sentences.zh: 而事实上，这则广告真正让你做的是

sentences.en: what the company wants you to do.
I mean, I remember in high school that there was a whole group of kids
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得在高中时，有一大群孩子

sentences.en: who would wear Metallica shirts, and they were trying to show how different they were,
sentences.zh: 会穿着金属乐队的衬衫，他们试图表现出自己的与众不同，

sentences.en: but yet they were all wearing Metallica shirts,
sentences.zh: 但他们却都穿着金属乐队的衬衫，

sentences.en: and so they were sort of, it sort of defeated the purpose on some level,
sentences.zh: 所以他们有点，这在某种程度上违背了初衷，

sentences.en: but it wasn't immediately apparent to them.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有马上意识到这一点。

sentences.en: One thing that Nero has found is that consumers are attracted
sentences.zh: 尼鲁发现的一件事是，吸引消费者的

sentences.en: not just to high-end brands, but to powerful brands.
sentences.zh: 不仅是高端品牌，还有强大的品牌。

sentences.en: Walmart can be a status symbol.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛也可以成为一种身份的象征。

sentences.en: So there's this relationship between status and power,
sentences.zh: 所以地位和权力之间存在着这样一种关系，

sentences.en: and so status is a way, it's sort of what we get when we have power.
sentences.zh: 地位可以说是我们拥有权力时所得到的东西。

sentences.en: And so when we think about power,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考权力时，

sentences.en: we can think about Walmart as being a really powerful brand.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把沃尔玛看作是一个非常具有影响力的品牌。

sentences.en: It has a lot of strength in the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 它在市场上有着很强的实力。

sentences.en: And so that strength, that kind of access to power,
sentences.zh: 这种实力，也就是对权力的这种获取，

sentences.en: having a lot of resources as a brand in itself,
sentences.zh: 作为品牌本身拥有大量的资源，

sentences.en: even though it's kind of a low-end brand,
sentences.zh: 尽管它某种程度上是一个低端品牌，

sentences.en: if you compare it to other low-end brands,
sentences.zh: 如果你把它与其他低端品牌进行比较，

sentences.en: that can be kind of attractive to people who care about status.
sentences.zh: 对于那些在意地位的人来说，这可能会很有吸引力。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to speak to Nero about how we use money
sentences.zh: 节目回来后，我将与尼罗谈谈我们如何使用金钱

sentences.en: not just to express our values, but to ignore them.
sentences.zh: 不仅来表达我们的价值观，甚至还用来忽视它们。

sentences.en: Many of us understand the economic choices we make
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都明白，我们所做出的经济选择
可能会带来真正的道德后果。

sentences.en: The products we buy can adversely affect the environment
sentences.zh: 我们购买的产品可能会对环境造成不利影响，

sentences.en: or take advantage of poor people in distant countries.
sentences.zh: 或者剥削遥远国家的穷人。

sentences.en: We can buy stuff from stores that treat their employees well,
sentences.zh: 我们可以从善待员工的商店购买东西，

sentences.en: or we can buy things, sometimes at a cheaper price,
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以从虐待员工的商店

sentences.en: from stores that treat their employees poorly.
sentences.zh: 购买东西，有时价格会更便宜。

sentences.en: Often, after a big news story about conditions in sweatshops
sentences.zh: 通常，在关于血汗工厂状况

sentences.en: or the use of child labor, there's public outrage.
sentences.zh: 或使用童工的大新闻报道之后，会引发公众的愤怒。

sentences.en: But as Neeru Paharia has explored,
sentences.zh: 但正如尼鲁·帕哈里亚所探讨的那样，

sentences.en: our actions don't always match our rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 我们的行动并不总是与我们的言辞相符。

sentences.en: She once wrote a paper on the subject titled,
sentences.zh: 她曾写过一篇关于这个主题的论文，题为

sentences.en: Sweatshop labor is wrong unless the shoes are cute.
